Modern.tagline: A food delivery service. Modern. Honest.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Doorbell is the moment of the food handoff — single archaic domestic word, immediately readable. Single-word naming follows the considered-modern delivery school (Caviar, Postmates of original era).
Modern.industrySummary: Modern food delivery has consolidated around three or four giants and a long tail of regional players. The customer is design-literate, increasingly tired of the platform-aesthetic sameness, and willing to pay more for a service that actually delivers the food intact.
Modern.competitorLandscape: DoorDash (doordash.com) holds the U.S. giant peer position. Uber Eats (ubereats.com) sits at the same tier. Wonder (wonder.com) does the modern verticalized middle. Grubhub (grubhub.com) is the older incumbent. We sit closer to Wonder in posture.
Modern.positioningStatement: A food delivery brand that competes on whether the food arrives intact.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 45. Orders food two or three times a week. Already pays for one premium delivery service. Will switch the moment one of them ships a soggy order.

dos: Show the delivery time and the temperature on the package
Speak to the customer as a person who just paid for food
Confirm orders in one short note
donts: Photograph delivery riders against neutral backdrops

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. Doorbell in a tight modern grotesk, all caps, two words on one line. A small geometric mark, two thin curves suggesting rising steam, used as the favicon and on every delivery bag seal.

typography.primary: Inter for product UI and headlines
typography.secondary: IBM Plex Mono for delivery times and prices
typography.rationale: Inter handles the marketing and app. The mono carries the times and prices.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No loyalty-tier upsell screens. No 'extra delivery insurance' add-on. No celebrity-restaurant marketing. No 'wellness meal' bundles.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: An app that books in three taps. Each order ships with a temperature-checked seal. A monthly email if the customer hasn't ordered in a while, written like a friend asking what they're eating.

Modern.brandDescription: A food delivery brand that competes on whether the food arrives intact.
Modern.mission: To build a food delivery brand that competes on whether the food arrives intact.
Modern.vision: The customer is design-literate, increasingly tired of the platform-aesthetic sameness, and willing to pay more for a service that actually delivers the food intact.
coreValues: Considered — we choose fewer things, more carefully.
Modern — we build for the customer reading this on a phone.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Two words. Saturday Delivery names a specific moment in the week that has always meant something: weekend, hosting, the bigger meal. The brand puts the highest-effort meal of the week in the brand position. Distinctive, slightly old-world, and immediately understood.
Luxury.story: Saturday Delivery began as a single delivery service for the kind of household that hosts properly on Saturdays. The founders had spent years inside larger catering companies and wanted to operate on a smaller, more careful schedule. The service operates only on Saturdays. The client list is small by design.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end food delivery has been dominated by tech-platform marketplaces. There's a parallel market for high-end private delivery services that operate like a household catering arrangement. Once-a-week service, small client list, real chefs and real ingredients delivered to a household that knows how to receive them.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Goldbelly (goldbelly.com) holds the institutional gourmet delivery peer position. Caviar (trycaviar.com) sits at the premium platform tier. Tock (exploretock.com) does the design-led booking middle. We sit smaller than all of them.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A weekly private delivery service for households that host properly.

targetAudience.primary: Wealthy. Often hosts Saturday dinners. Has a regular catering arrangement they're tired of. Wants a single service that handles the food, the wine, and the timing.

dos: Send a paper card the week before

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small hand-drawn clock-hand hallmark, pointing to a notional Saturday afternoon, used on the order book, the delivery boxes, and the wax seal of every paper letter.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and printed material
typography.secondary: Söhne for the secure ordering portal
typography.rationale: A high contrast classical serif sets the heritage tone. A modern grotesk handles the few digital surfaces.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No weeknight delivery. No third-party platforms. No marketing emails. No social media. No public price list.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Single word. Drop is the moment of delivery, the verb the driver uses, and the noun for what arrives. The brand names the smallest unit of the service, plain and unadorned.
Minimal.industrySummary: Most food delivery brands have elaborate names and ambitious brand worlds. There's an opening for one that strips it back to the moment the food arrives.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most food delivery brands fail this purity test. The closest peers in spirit are some Japanese delivery services and certain Scandinavian grocery delivery aesthetics.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A food delivery service named after the moment it works.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who want food delivered and don't need a relationship with the platform. They want the order, the time, the receipt.

dos: Show the time, the restaurant, the price
Send a single SMS at delivery

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Two words. Crosstown is the urban-delivery verb every dispatcher uses. The brand is named after the work, not the holding company. Co. closes it as a real, established firm. Distinctive without the 'Logistics Group' template.
Corporate.industrySummary: Last-mile food logistics is a B2B category serving restaurant groups, grocery chains, and corporate cafeteria operators. Buyers are operations directors who want a reliable delivery partner that integrates with their existing systems.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: DoorDash Drive (doordash.com/drive) holds the platform-led last-mile peer position. Relay (relaydeliveries.com) sits in the restaurant-services tier. Cut+Dry (cutanddry.com) does the food-distribution middle. We sit smaller and more focused on the contemporary urban restaurant operator side.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Last-mile food logistics for restaurant groups and grocery chains in dense urban markets.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Urban restaurant groups want delivery partners with operational discipline and clean technology. The platform giants don't integrate well. We sit between them.

targetAudience.primary: Operations Directors, COOs, and Logistics Directors at restaurant groups, grocery chains, and corporate cafeteria operators. They sign multi-year contracts.

Creative.brandNameRationale: The Twelve Plate is a restaurant trade phrase for the last full table service of the night. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school.
Creative.manifesto: Most food delivery brands sell convenience, speed, and growth. We made Late Dinner because the truth about ordering food is that it's mostly a small private moment. The lights are low. The day is over. The person at the door is tired. We are the brand for the meal that nobody else made, at the hour nobody else is awake.
Creative.industrySummary: Food delivery branding has been polished, optimization-led, and slightly cold. There's room for a brand that's warm, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and serious about the actual emotional moment of ordering food at night.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Caviar (trycaviar.com) holds the premium-food delivery peer. Postmates (postmates.com) sits at the lifestyle tier. Resy at Home (resy.com) does the restaurant-experience middle. We sit warmer and more honest than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A food delivery brand for the small private meal at the end of the day.
